identity.title: Is the Doctrine of Purgatory True? Trent Horn vs. James White (2024)
identity.label: Purgatory and postmortem purification
identity.motion: Is the doctrine of purgatory true?

pro.name: The doctrine of purgatory is true
pro.speaker: Trent Horn

con.name: The doctrine of purgatory is false
con.speaker: James White

routes.speaker: Trent Horn
routes.position: The doctrine of purgatory is true

bridges.statement: Christ completes the sanctification and correction of saved persons before the beatific vision.
Purgatory is passive divine purification, not a second chance or self-salvation.
Saved persons imperfect at death must be cleansed before heaven.
God may complete unpleasant fatherly correction after death.
Matthew, Corinthian judgment, and afterlife texts permit postmortem purification or consequences.
Grace, derivative merit, and finite consequences do not replace Christ's saving work.
Jewish and early Christian evidence supplies continuity for a postmortem purifying core.

routes.speaker: James White
routes.position: The doctrine of purgatory is false

bridges.statement: Christ's imputed righteousness and complete saving work exclude purgatory as a condition of righteous standing.
The historic doctrine includes temporal punishment, satisfaction, merit, and indulgences rather than mere sanctification.
The cited Matthew and Corinthian texts concern legal warning, ministry, works, or final judgment rather than purgatory.
Believers possess a new nature and enter Christ's presence directly through faith.
Purgatory arose through diverse and late historical development rather than apostolic continuity.
Hebrews' fatherly discipline operates during earthly Christian life.
